question: What undergraduate engineering courses are offered at DKTE Ichalkaranji?
short_answer_speech: DKTE offers 12 approved B.Tech programs, including Computer Science, CSE with AI and Machine Learning, Electronics and Telecommunication, AI and Data Science, Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, and our world-renowned Textile programs such as Textile Technology and Fashion Technology.
detailed_answer: DKTE Society's Textile and Engineering Institute offers 12 undergraduate B.Tech courses: 1) Computer Science & Engineering (120 seats), 2) CSE - AI & ML (120 seats), 3) Electronics & Telecommunication (120 seats), 4) AI & Data Science (60 seats), 5) Mechanical Engineering (60 seats), 6) Electrical Engineering (60 seats), 7) Civil Engineering (60 seats), 8) Textile Technology (60 seats), 9) Textile Chemistry (60 seats), 10) Man-Made Textile Technology (30 seats), 11) Fashion Technology (30 seats), and 12) Technical Textiles (30 seats). All courses are AICTE approved and affiliated with Shivaji University, Kolhapur.

question: What is the intake capacity for Computer Science and Engineering at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: The intake for B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering is 120 seats. We also offer 120 seats in CSE with AI & Machine Learning, and 60 seats in AI & Data Science.
detailed_answer: The approved intake capacity for First Year B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering (DTE Choice Code: 622224210) is 120 seats. In addition, DKTE offers Computer Science and Engineering (Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning) with 120 seats, and Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Data Science with 60 seats, making a total of 300 computing-focused seats.

question: Is DKTE an autonomous institute or affiliated with a university?
short_answer_speech: DKTE is an Autonomous Institute, established in 1982 and affiliated with Shivaji University, Kolhapur. Autonomy allows us to design industry-ready curriculum and conduct timely exams.
detailed_answer: DKTE Society's Textile & Engineering Institute has been an Autonomous Institute since 2011, affiliated with Shivaji University, Kolhapur. It holds an 'A+' Grade accreditation from NAAC and NBA accreditation for its eligible engineering programs. Autonomy gives DKTE freedom to update its curriculum dynamically with industry experts while degrees are conferred by Shivaji University.

question: Why is DKTE especially famous for Textile Engineering?
short_answer_speech: DKTE is recognized across India and globally as a Centre of Excellence in Technical Textiles, appointed by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, with world-class pilot plants and 100% placement track records.
detailed_answer: DKTE was founded in Ichalkaranji (known as the 'Manchester of Maharashtra') in 1982 to advance textile education. It is recognized as a Centre of Excellence in Technical Textiles by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India. The institute houses state-of-the-art spinning, weaving, non-woven fabric pilot plants, and NABL-accredited testing laboratories, attracting recruiters worldwide.

question: Does DKTE offer postgraduate programs like M.Tech and MBA?
short_answer_speech: Yes, DKTE offers M.Tech in 5 specialized branches, an MBA program with 120 seats, and an MCA program with 60 seats.
detailed_answer: Yes, DKTE offers M.Tech programs (12 seats each) in Textile Engineering, Computer Science & Engineering, Electronics & Telecommunication, Mechanical Engineering (Product Design & Development), and Defence Technology. It also offers Master of Business Administration (MBA) with an intake of 120 seats and Master of Computer Applications (MCA) with 60 seats.

question: Does the college offer diploma courses after 10th standard?
short_answer_speech: Yes, our polytechnic wing offers 3-year diplomas in Textile Manufactures, Textile Technology, and Fashion and Clothing Technology under DTE code 6225.
detailed_answer: Yes, DKTE's polytechnic wing (DTE Institute Code: 6225) offers 3-year polytechnic diploma courses: Diploma in Textile Manufactures (60 seats), Diploma in Textile Technology (30 seats), and Diploma in Fashion and Clothing Technology (30 seats), approved by MSBTE Mumbai and AICTE.

question: What is the DTE institute code for DKTE in the Maharashtra engineering admission form?
short_answer_speech: The DTE choice code for DKTE degree engineering is 6222. You should search for 6222 in your State CET Cell option form.
detailed_answer: The official DTE Institute Code for D.K.T.E. Society's Textile & Engineering Institute, Ichalkaranji for First Year B.Tech and Direct Second Year Engineering is 6222. For diploma courses, the institute operates under DTE Code 6225.

question: What is the total annual fee for Open or General category students in B.Tech?
short_answer_speech: For Open category students, the annual fee approved by the Fee Regulating Authority is approximately 1,21,000 rupees, which includes 1,05,217 rupees tuition fee and 15,783 rupees development fee. Adding exam and insurance fees, total payable is around 1,25,000 rupees per year.
detailed_answer: The Fee Regulating Authority (FRA) Maharashtra approved fee structure for First Year B.Tech at DKTE (DTE 6222) is: Tuition Fee: ₹1,05,217; Development Fee: ₹15,783; making the approved college fee ₹1,21,000. Including university examination, gymkhana, and student insurance fees (~₹4,000), the total payable annual fee for Open/General category is approximately ₹1,25,000. In addition, a one-time refundable caution money deposit of ₹1,000 is charged at the time of admission.

question: How much fees do OBC and EBC category students need to pay for B.Tech?
short_answer_speech: OBC and EBC students with parental income up to 8 Lakh rupees receive a 50% tuition fee waiver from the government. They pay approximately 72,400 rupees per year instead of 1,25,000 rupees.
detailed_answer: For OBC (Other Backward Class) and EBC (Economically Backward Class / EWS) students admitted through CAP with annual parental income up to ₹8,00,000: 50% of the Tuition Fee (₹52,609) is reimbursed by the Maharashtra State Government. The student only pays 50% Tuition Fee (₹52,608) + 100% Development Fee (₹15,783) + Exam/University fees (~₹4,000), making the total annual payable fee approximately ₹72,392.

question: What are the fees for SC and ST students at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: For SC and ST students admitted through CAP, both tuition fee and development fee are 100% waived by the government. The student only pays nominal university examination and registration fees of around 4,000 rupees per year.
detailed_answer: Under the Government of India Post-Matric Scholarship administered by Social Justice & Special Assistance Department and Tribal Development Department, 100% of both Tuition and Development fees are waived for eligible SC and ST students admitted via CAP. They only need to pay nominal examination, enrollment, and student insurance fees amounting to approximately ₹4,000 per year.

question: What is the fee for students allotted a seat under TFWS (Tuition Fee Waiver Scheme)?
short_answer_speech: Students allotted under TFWS pay zero tuition fee throughout their 4 years. They only pay the development fee and examination charges, which comes to around 19,800 rupees per year.
detailed_answer: Under the AICTE / DTE Tuition Fee Waiver Scheme (TFWS), 100% of the Tuition Fee (₹1,05,217) is waived for all four years. The student is required to pay only the Development Fee (₹15,783) plus university examination and activity fees (~₹4,000), totaling approximately ₹19,783 per year.

question: Is there any free education or fee concession for girl students in engineering?
short_answer_speech: Yes, under the Maharashtra Government's Free Higher Education for Girls policy, female students admitted via CAP with family income up to 8 Lakh rupees receive a 100% tuition fee waiver, paying only development and exam fees around 19,800 rupees.
detailed_answer: Yes. Under the Maharashtra State Government Higher & Technical Education policy for girl students with annual family income up to ₹8,00,000 admitted through CAP: 100% of the Tuition Fee (₹1,05,217) is covered by the state government. The female student is only liable to pay the Development Fee (₹15,783) and nominal university charges (~₹4,000), totaling around ₹19,783 per year.

question: Can we pay the college fee in installments?
short_answer_speech: College fees are normally payable annually at the time of admission, but parents facing financial hardship can request two semester installments with prior written permission from the Accounts Office.
detailed_answer: Fees are generally payable in full at the time of admission confirmation via online ERP portal, Net Banking, or Demand Draft. However, students experiencing genuine financial difficulties can submit an application to the Accounts Department requesting payment in two semester-wise installments, subject to approval by the Director.

question: What payment modes are accepted for paying college fees at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: You can pay fees online through the DKTE Parent ERP portal using Net Banking, UPI, or Debit/Credit card, or submit a Demand Draft in favor of 'Director, DKTE Society's TEI, Ichalkaranji' at the college fee counter.
detailed_answer: DKTE accepts: 1) Online payment through the official DKTE ERP Parent Portal via Net Banking, Debit Card, Credit Card, or UPI; 2) Demand Draft (DD) drawn in favor of 'Director, DKTE Society's TEI, Ichalkaranji' payable at Ichalkaranji; 3) Point-of-Sale (POS) card swipe at the college accounts counter. Cash transactions above nominal limits are not encouraged as per government audit norms.

question: Can I get admission to B.Tech without appearing for MHT-CET?
short_answer_speech: Yes, if you have appeared for JEE Main Paper-1, you can apply under the 15% All India Quota through Maharashtra CAP, or apply for Institute Level Quota. Appearing in either MHT-CET or JEE Main is mandatory.
detailed_answer: Candidates cannot be considered for First Year B.Tech admissions without appearing in either MHT-CET (PCM) or JEE Main (Paper-1). For Maharashtra State quota seats (65%), MHT-CET score is mandatory. For All India seats (15%) and Institute Level quota (20%), candidates with valid JEE Main or MHT-CET scores are eligible.

question: What is the minimum 12th board percentage required for engineering admission?
short_answer_speech: You need at least 45% marks in Physics, Mathematics and one optional technical subject for Open category, and at least 40% marks if you belong to a reserved category from Maharashtra.
detailed_answer: Candidates must have passed HSC (Std. XII) with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects, along with one of Chemistry, Biotechnology, Biology, or a Technical Vocational subject. The minimum aggregate in these three subjects must be at least 45% for General/Open category, and at least 40% for Backward Class categories, EWS, and Persons with Disability belonging to Maharashtra State.

question: How are seats distributed between CAP and Management or Institute Quota at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: At DKTE, 65% of seats are Maharashtra State CAP seats, 15% are All India CAP seats based on JEE Main, and 20% are Institute Level merit seats.
detailed_answer: The seat matrix for First Year B.Tech at DKTE is structured as: 1) 65% Maharashtra State (MS) seats filled through Centralized Admission Process (CAP) based on MHT-CET percentile; 2) 15% All India (AI) seats filled through CAP based on JEE Main Paper-1 or MHT-CET; 3) 20% Institute Level (IL) / Management Quota seats filled transparently on merit at the college level adhering to CET Cell guidelines. In addition, 5% TFWS and 10% EWS supernumerary seats are offered.

question: What is the eligibility for Direct Second Year B.Tech (Lateral Entry)?
short_answer_speech: Diploma holders with at least 45% marks (40% for reserved categories) or B.Sc. graduates with Mathematics in 12th are eligible for direct second year engineering through CAP rounds.
detailed_answer: For Direct Second Year (DSE) B.Tech: Candidates must have passed a Diploma in Engineering & Technology from an AICTE or MSBTE approved institution with at least 45% aggregate marks (40% for Backward Class categories, EWS, and PwD candidates of Maharashtra State). Alternatively, candidates who completed a B.Sc. Degree with at least 45% marks and Mathematics at 10+2 level are also eligible.

question: How do I apply for the 20% Institute Level Quota seats at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: To apply for Institute Level seats, you must register on the Maharashtra State CET Cell portal, get your documents verified, and then submit our college institutional application form online or in person.
detailed_answer: To apply for the 20% Institute Level / Vacancy Quota seats: 1) Candidates must have registered with the State CET Cell and possess a valid Merit Number; 2) Visit the DKTE Admissions Office or portal during the notified institutional round; 3) Fill out the Institute Level application form and attach verified document copies; 4) Admissions are granted strictly based on merit ranks as per government guidelines.

question: What is the step-by-step process for CAP round admissions?
short_answer_speech: First register on the State CET Cell website, complete document verification at a Scrutiny Centre, fill your college option form giving DKTE choice code 6222, accept your allotted seat, and report to DKTE to confirm admission.
detailed_answer: The CAP admission process follows these stages: 1) Online registration on mahacet.org portal; 2) Document verification through e-Scrutiny or Physical Scrutiny Centers; 3) Display of Provisional and Final Merit Lists; 4) Submission and confirmation of Option Form with DKTE Choice Codes (e.g., 622224210 for CSE); 5) Seat Allotment by CET Cell; 6) Seat Acceptance via portal and payment of seat acceptance fee; 7) Physical reporting to DKTE with original documents to finalize admission.

question: Can students from other states outside Maharashtra get admission to DKTE?
short_answer_speech: Yes, outside Maharashtra students can secure admission under the 15% All India Quota through CAP based on JEE Main scores, or apply for Institute Level Quota seats.
detailed_answer: Yes, candidates residing outside Maharashtra State (OMS) are eligible for admission through: 1) The 15% All India Quota seats conducted in CAP rounds by State CET Cell on the basis of valid JEE Main Paper-1 percentile; 2) The 20% Institute Level Quota merit seats. OMS candidates need an Eligibility Certificate from Shivaji University and a Migration Certificate.

question: Is there any management donation required for admission at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: No, DKTE does not charge any donation. All admissions, including Institute Level seats, are strictly merit-based following approved government fee structures.
detailed_answer: No donation or capitation fee is charged at DKTE. All seats, including CAP and Institute Level quota seats, are allotted purely on merit based on MHT-CET and JEE Main scores in compliance with the Maharashtra Prohibition of Capitation Fee Act and Fee Regulating Authority directives.

question: What scholarships can I apply for through the MahaDBT portal at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: You can apply for the EBC scholarship, Girls Free Education scheme, Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Hostel allowance, and post-matric scholarships for SC, ST, OBC, VJ-NT, and SBC categories.
detailed_answer: Through the Government of Maharashtra MahaDBT portal (mahadbt.maharashtra.gov.in), DKTE students can apply for: 1) Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj Shikshan Shulkh Shishyavrutti Yojna (EBC - 50% tuition waiver for Open category with income <= 8 LPA); 2) Girls Higher Education 100% Tuition Fee Waiver; 3) Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Hostel Maintenance Allowance; 4) Post-Matric Scholarships/Freeships for SC, ST, VJ-NT, SBC, and OBC categories; 5) State Government Minority Scholarships.

question: What is the family income limit to be eligible for the EBC scholarship?
short_answer_speech: The annual family income must be 8 Lakh rupees or less from all sources, certified by a Tahsildar or Sub-Divisional Officer.
detailed_answer: Under the Rajarshi Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj Shikshan Shulkh Shishyavrutti Yojna (EBC), the annual parental income from all sources must not exceed ₹8,00,000. An authentic Income Certificate issued by a competent revenue authority (Tahsildar or SDO) for the current financial year is mandatory.

question: What is the Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Hostel Allowance and how much is given?
short_answer_speech: It provides hostel maintenance allowance of up to 20,000 rupees per year for students staying in hostels or paying guest accommodation away from home with family income up to 8 Lakh rupees.
detailed_answer: The Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Vastigruh Nirvah Bhatta Yojna offers maintenance allowance up to ₹20,000 per year (for 10 months @ ₹2,000/month) for students studying in Ichalkaranji whose parents' annual income is up to ₹8,00,000 and who reside in recognized hostels or registered paying guest facilities away from their native taluka. For children of registered marginal farmers and construction workers, enhanced benefits are available.

question: Does the college assist in obtaining bank education loans?
short_answer_speech: Yes, our student section assists students with bonafide certificates and fee estimates for bank education loans and supports the Vidya Lakshmi education loan portal.
detailed_answer: Yes, DKTE provides comprehensive support for educational loans through the Government of India's Vidya Lakshmi Portal (vidyalakshmi.co.in) and maintains institutional relationships with nationalized banks (SBI, Bank of Maharashtra, Canara Bank, Union Bank). The Student Section promptly issues Fee Structure Certificates and Bonafide Certificates needed for loan sanctioning.

question: Do M.Tech students get a monthly stipend at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: Yes, GATE-qualified M.Tech students receive an AICTE PG scholarship of 12,400 rupees per month for 24 months.
detailed_answer: Candidates who have qualified GATE and are admitted to approved M.Tech programs at DKTE are eligible to receive the AICTE Post Graduate Scholarship of ₹12,400 per month for the complete 24-month program duration, subject to attendance and performance conditions specified by AICTE.

question: What happens if a reserved category student fails to submit their MahaDBT scholarship form?
short_answer_speech: If a student fails to submit the scholarship form on the MahaDBT portal on time, the government will not reimburse the fees, and the student will have to pay full Open category fees.
detailed_answer: As per Directorate of Technical Education and Social Welfare directives, submitting the online scholarship/freeship application on the MahaDBT portal within the stipulated deadline is mandatory for all reserved category (SC/ST/OBC/VJNT/SBC/EBC) students. If a student fails to submit the form or if the application is rejected due to invalid documents, the student is personally liable to pay full Open category institutional fees.

question: Are minority community students eligible for special scholarships at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: Yes, students from Jain, Muslim, Christian, Buddhist, Sikh, and Parsi communities with income under 8 Lakhs can apply for the State Minority Scholarship of up to 50,000 rupees per year.
detailed_answer: Yes. Eligible students belonging to notified religious minority communities (Jain, Muslim, Buddhist, Christian, Sikh, Parsi) with annual family income up to ₹8,00,000 admitted through CAP can apply for the Government of Maharashtra State Minority Scholarship, which awards financial assistance of up to ₹50,000 per year towards tuition and course expenses.

question: What are the hostel options available for boys and girls at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: DKTE provides separate campus hostels for boys with a capacity of 50 students and girls with a capacity of 324 students, equipped with Wi-Fi, solar heating, and 24x7 security.
detailed_answer: DKTE maintains separate, well-maintained residential hostels: 1) Boys Hostel: Accommodates approximately 50 students across 20 rooms in twin and triple sharing configurations; 2) Girls Hostel: Accommodates approximately 324 students across 90 rooms with 3-seater and 4-seater options, complete with dedicated reading halls, biometric entry, and round-the-clock female wardens.

question: What is the annual hostel fee and mess charges at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: The hostel accommodation fee is approximately 25,000 rupees per year, and the mess charges are around 33,000 rupees per year for daily nutritious vegetarian meals.
detailed_answer: The annual accommodation fee for DKTE Boys and Girls Hostels is approximately ₹25,000 per year (plus a refundable caution deposit of ₹2,000). The campus mess charges are approximately ₹33,000 per year (averaging ~₹2,750 per month) for 4 daily meals (breakfast, lunch, evening tea, and dinner).

question: What security and safety measures are in place at the Girls Hostel?
short_answer_speech: The girls hostel has 24x7 security guards, CCTV surveillance, biometric attendance, resident female wardens, a medical clinic, and a strict 8:00 PM evening curfew.
detailed_answer: Safety at the Girls Hostel is treated with highest priority: 1) Round-the-clock security personnel at entry gates; 2) Full CCTV coverage of perimeters, corridors, and entryways; 3) Biometric attendance access control; 4) Resident full-time female wardens living on-premises; 5) Strict 8:00 PM evening in-time rule; 6) Medical first-aid room with visiting lady doctor; 7) Emergency parental notification system.

question: What kind of food is served in the college mess, and can we opt out of the mess?
short_answer_speech: The mess serves hygienic pure vegetarian Indian meals. For campus hostel residents, enrolling in the mess is compulsory to ensure student health and nutrition.
detailed_answer: The DKTE mess serves hygienic pure-vegetarian food, including seasonal vegetables, dal, chapati, rice, curd, and special weekend feasts. Cleanliness is monitored by a faculty-led Hostel & Mess Committee. For all residents staying inside college hostels, mess membership is mandatory for health, hygiene, and community living standards.

question: What are the library facilities and operating hours at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: The central library has over 65,000 books, digital IEEE and ScienceDirect journals, and a 350-seat reading hall that stays open 24 hours during exam periods.
detailed_answer: The Dr. K. B. Powar Central Knowledge Centre houses over 65,000 volumes, national/international print journals, and online digital subscriptions to IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, and Delnet. It features a digital library lab with internet terminals, a book bank scheme for needy students, and large reading halls open from 8:00 AM to 10:00 PM on regular days and 24 hours during end-semester examinations.

question: Does the campus have Wi-Fi and modern computer laboratories?
short_answer_speech: Yes, the campus has 1 Gbps high-speed leased line Wi-Fi and over 1,200 computers with specialized labs for Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, and Textile CAD.
detailed_answer: Yes. DKTE features a high-speed optical fiber backbone with 1 Gbps dedicated leased-line internet connectivity and secure Wi-Fi access throughout academic buildings and hostels. There are over 1,200 computers equipped with industry-standard software such as MATLAB, ANSYS, SolidWorks, Cadence, and specialized Textile CAD suites.

question: What sports and gymnasium facilities are available on campus?
short_answer_speech: The college has a modern gymnasium, indoor badminton and table tennis courts, and large outdoor grounds for cricket, football, basketball, and volleyball.
detailed_answer: The institute provides a full-fledged gymnasium with modern cardio and weight training equipment, indoor facilities for table tennis, carrom, chess, and badminton, as well as spacious outdoor sports grounds for cricket, volleyball, football, and basketball. Students regularly represent Shivaji University in zonal and state level tournaments.

question: What was the highest and average salary package offered in recent DKTE campus placements?
short_answer_speech: In the recent academic cycle, the highest package was 16.5 Lakh rupees per year, with an overall average package of 4.85 Lakh rupees per year, and peak offers reaching up to 15 to 45 Lakhs in specialized tech drives.
detailed_answer: For the 2023-2024 academic cycle, DKTE recorded a highest on-campus package of ₹16.5 LPA and an average package of ₹4.85 LPA across branches. Over the years, select off-campus and niche technology drives have reached peak packages of up to ₹15 to ₹45 LPA. Core textile engineering graduates consistently achieve near 100% placement with reputed multinational apparel brands.

question: Which major IT and software companies recruit from DKTE?
short_answer_speech: Top recruiters include TCS, Infosys, Cognizant, Capgemini, Persistent Systems, Tech Mahindra, KPIT Technologies, and L&T Technology Services.
detailed_answer: Major IT services, software, and consulting recruiters visiting DKTE include: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys Technologies, Cognizant, Capgemini, Persistent Systems, Tech Mahindra, Wipro, Accenture, KPIT, and L&T Infotech. These companies recruit from CSE, AI & ML, AI & DS, and ENTC branches.

question: Which core companies hire textile and mechanical engineering students from DKTE?
short_answer_speech: Textile students are hired by Raymond, Welspun, Aditya Birla Group, Arvind Mills, and Vardhman, while mechanical students are placed in Tata Motors, Cummins India, and Bosch.
detailed_answer: For Textile and Allied branches, premier recruiters include Raymond Limited, Aditya Birla Group (Grasim & Linen Club), Welspun India, Vardhman Textiles, Arvind Mills, Trident Group, Himatsingka, and Alok Industries. For Mechanical, Electrical, and Civil disciplines, regular recruiters include Tata Motors, Cummins India, Bharat Forge, Thermax, Kirloskar, and L&T.

question: What is the overall placement percentage at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: DKTE maintains a consistent placement record of around 83% to 86% across eligible graduating students, with Textile branches reaching 100% placement.
detailed_answer: Over the last three consecutive academic years, DKTE has maintained an impressive placement track record: 82.94% in 2023-2024 (564 students placed out of 680 eligible), 85.84% in 2022-2023, and 86.29% in 2021-2022. Textile Technology and Fashion Technology branches frequently achieve 100% campus placement due to high industrial demand.

question: Does the college provide campus placement training and internship support?
short_answer_speech: Yes, our Training and Placement Cell conducts soft skills, aptitude training, coding bootcamps, and arranges compulsory semester internships with leading companies.
detailed_answer: Yes, the Training and Placement Cell organizes structured training starting from the second year: 1) Quantitative aptitude and logical reasoning classes; 2) Coding workshops in Python, Java, and Data Structures; 3) Mock interviews and group discussions; 4) Industry internships in semester breaks led by Central Internship In-charge Dr. S. J. Patil.

question: Who can I contact regarding campus placements and internships at DKTE?
short_answer_speech: You can contact Prof. G. S. Joshi for Engineering placements at 9422619947, or Mr. S. B. Akiwate for Textile placements at 9766562001.
detailed_answer: For Engineering Disciplines, contact Training & Placement Officer Prof. G. S. Joshi at +91 9422619947 or email dktetpo@gmail.com. For Textile Disciplines, contact TPO Mr. S. B. Akiwate at +91 9766562001 or email sanjay.akiwate@dktes.com. For central internships, contact Dr. S. J. Patil at +91 8275002239.

question: What original documents are required at the time of engineering admission?
short_answer_speech: You need your MHT-CET or JEE scorecard, 10th and 12th mark sheets, school leaving certificate, domicile certificate, income certificate, caste and validity certificates if applicable, Aadhaar card, and 5 photographs.
detailed_answer: Mandatory documents required for First Year B.Tech admission reporting at DKTE: 1) MHT-CET or JEE Main Score Card; 2) HSC (12th) Mark Sheet; 3) SSC (10th) Mark Sheet; 4) Original School/College Leaving Certificate (Transfer Certificate); 5) Maharashtra State Domicile & Nationality Certificate (or Birth Certificate); 6) Aadhaar Card photocopy; 7) 5 Passport-size photographs. For reserved categories: Caste Certificate, Caste Validity Certificate, and Non-Creamy Layer (NCL) Certificate.

question: Is Caste Validity Certificate compulsory at the time of admission for OBC or SC students?
short_answer_speech: Yes, Caste Validity Certificate is strictly compulsory. Without it, you cannot claim category benefits and your seat will be converted to Open category as per government rules.
detailed_answer: Yes, under Maharashtra State Government rules, submission of a valid Caste Validity Certificate issued by the Divisional Caste Scrutiny Committee is strictly mandatory at the time of admission for SC, ST, VJ-NT, SBC, and OBC category students. Failure to produce the validity certificate results in forfeiture of the reserved category seat or conversion to Open category with full fees.

question: What is a Non-Creamy Layer (NCL) certificate and who needs it?
short_answer_speech: Non-Creamy Layer certificate is mandatory for OBC, VJ-NT, and SBC category candidates to prove parental income is under 8 Lakhs, and it must be valid for the current financial year.
detailed_answer: The Non-Creamy Layer (NCL) certificate verifies that the candidate's family income does not exceed the creamy layer threshold (₹8,00,000 per annum). It is mandatory for candidates claiming reservation under VJ/DT-NT(A), NT(B), NT(C), NT(D), SBC, and OBC categories. The certificate must be explicitly valid up to 31st March of the ongoing academic cycle. SC and ST candidates do not require an NCL certificate.

question: If I have a gap after 12th standard, what document do I need to submit?
short_answer_speech: You need to submit an Educational Gap Affidavit on a 100-rupee stamp paper attested by a Notary Public explaining the reason for your gap year.
detailed_answer: Candidates who have taken a break in their education between passing Class XII (or qualifying diploma) and seeking engineering admission must submit an original Gap Affidavit on a ₹100 stamp paper attested by a Notary Public or Executive Magistrate, certifying that they did not join any other degree college during the intervening period.

question: Do CBSE or other out-of-state board students need a Migration Certificate?
short_answer_speech: Yes, students from CBSE, ICSE, or outside Maharashtra boards must submit an original Migration Certificate from their board to complete university registration.
detailed_answer: Yes. Candidates who have passed their qualifying examination (12th Std. or Diploma) from a board or university other than the Maharashtra State Board (such as CBSE, CISCE, NIOS, or out-of-state boards) must submit an original Migration Certificate to obtain an Eligibility Certificate from Shivaji University, Kolhapur.

question: Does the college retain original documents after admission?
short_answer_speech: Yes, original mark sheets, leaving certificate, and category certificates are retained for university verification and returned after university approval, while verified copies are given back immediately.
detailed_answer: As per Directorate of Technical Education and Shivaji University norms, original qualifying certificates (Leaving Certificate, Mark sheets, Domicile, Caste/Validity certificates) are temporarily retained by the college student section for formal verification by the University Eligibility Section. Once verified, all certificates except the Leaving Certificate are returned to the student, and an official document receipt is provided upon admission.

question: When does the engineering admission registration start each year?
short_answer_speech: Engineering registration on the State CET Cell portal usually begins in mid-June following the declaration of MHT-CET results, with CAP rounds running through July and August.
detailed_answer: Engineering admissions in Maharashtra follow the Centralized Admission Process (CAP) conducted by the State CET Cell. Online registration and document verification generally commence in the third week of June, with Round 1, Round 2, and Round 3 choice filling and seat allotments spanning across July and August. Institutional reporting concludes before the mandatory cut-off date.

question: Can a student report for admission after the CAP reporting deadline has passed?
short_answer_speech: No, if you miss the reporting deadline on the CET Cell portal, your allotted seat is automatically cancelled by the system, so you must report before the cut-off date.
detailed_answer: No. Seat allotment in CAP rounds is strictly governed by CET Cell portal timestamps. If a candidate fails to accept the seat online and report to the allotted institute with required documents and fees within the published schedule, the allotment is automatically treated as cancelled, and the vacant seat is made available for subsequent rounds.
